description.narrative: In ASEAN, a substantial share of informal economy is in the agri-food sector, particularly in Laos there are a lots of small-scale agricultural cultivation and food processing-sales sector. they should be regarded as workers who are entitled to decent work including good social protection. although, the percentage of employment in agricultural sector has decreased (to 59% in Laos in 2018) , but can be said that this group still account for the large proportion of informal workers, which get hired with low pay, insufficient and has low potential. Mostly, MSMES in Laos, the agricultural sector employs 99,1% of the workforce, while 88% of jobs in rural areas are in the informal sector. Majority of the workers are women and children, who work for their family businesses as unpaid labour. There are more than 7 millions people with 18 provinces and 143 districts in Laos, an average of GDP growth rate of 5,8% per year. Informal workers mark up to 83% of labour force and are the significant factor in the country’s economic and social development.According to the findings of joint research conducted by Asian Development Bank (ADB) and International Labour Organisation (ILO), there are still significant number of workers who earn daily pay, have precarious employment and not covered by social welfare or social protection. Particularly, the most impacted are women workers in the informal economic sector who are disadvantaged and vulnerable in socioeconomic terms, which includes self-employed, small-scaled farmers, migrant workers, unemployed workers and others due to the relevant parties still lack of decent policies and effective enforcement in promoting decent employment as well as social protection system. Government of Laos is aware of this issues and has taken into crucial consideration to promote and implement social protection policies, such as the adoption of “ASEAN DECLARATION ON STREGNTHENING SOCIAL PROTECTION” by the Lao PDR in October 2014, which recognize equal access to social protection as a fundamental human right. The declaration was supported by the guidelines of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) R202 (Social Protection Floor) and the push to execute the policy to achieve four key objectives, such as Universal Health Coverage (UHC); child income security, elderly income security and working age workers. This aims to enhance, access to well-being and live a decent life by their life cycle and specifically looking back to capture various adverse issues. In addition, ASEAN has developed the “ASEAN plans and Action plans for Implementation of the Resource plan on strengthening social protection. Relevant committees and related ministries were established in accordance with the action plans to encourage, support and oversee members regarding the designs, resource contribution and development of national policy plan for social protection. Based upon the mentioned issues and circumstances, this project is intended to effectively assist the growth of social protection for the interests of vulnerable workers (informal workers) and their families. It aims to contribute to the development of local, national and international policies and practices addressing social protection to enhance accessibility to public service systems as well as to contribute to the government and international ending poverty. The project focuses on ADVANCING SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WORKERS IN THE AGRI-FOOD SECTOR IN THE LAO PDR in order to comply with the government policies. The project will work in close cooperation with the Lao Federation of Trade Union (LFTU) from central to local levels to enable informal workers to access and perceive social protection information policy set out by the government such as social security law, health insurance including the socual welfare policy that protect low-income workers are all designed to encourage voluntary social security enrollment and provide accessibility to high-quality, cost-free healthcare, handing vulnerable workers some peace of mind in the event of illness.

participating-org.narrative:
the mission statement of MHP, MHP seeks to build the capacity of the people, and poor women in rural areas in particular, so that they have a higher quality of life, in which they can take control of their destiny in sustainable ways. This includes theproper management of non-timber forest products which can be used to improve income and ensure food security and nutrition for mothers and children. At the same time, there is a need to create awareness of gender issues, children’s and women’s rights andprotection of the local environment. Finally, MHP aspires to build the capacity of government staff associated with development work in Bokeo, as well as being part of a learning network for the northern provinces of Laos or throughout the country.
Maeying Huamjai Phattana (translated as women mobilising for development) or MHP, is a new non profit association (or NPA) organisation which has been formed under the recently passed decree on associations (dated April 29th 2009) .
MHP was founded inMarch 2010, when it received approval to form a steering committee for the purposes of seeking registration as an NPA from the Bokeo provincial government. It received official approval as a licensed NPA on 9th July 2010. Its Director, Ms Vansy Senyavong,was previously employed by VECO, while four of VECO’s expected to become MHP staff by the end of 2010. Although there will be some continuity in some areas of the VECO program, it should be recognised that MHP is an independent Lao organisation with a new agenda.
VECO is a Belgian INGO that seeks to improve the livelihoods of family farmers through sustainable agriculture chain development. It started work in Laos in 2002, with food securityprograms in Meung and Paktha districts, and in 2007 startedvalue chain development activities with local farmer organisations in Houayxay, Tonpheung, Paktha and Meung districts. For more information, see www.vredeseilanden.be
MHP takes women, and especially rural and ethnic women, as the starting point. TheMHP team felt that women needed to be given special priority if Bokeo is to develop its development potential. This position was reinforced during the development of the mission and goals of MHP, during which experience was exchanged with other successfully operating NPA’s in Lao PDR, and with Gender Development Group (GDG) and Normai in particular.
